36805765.summary: In mice given cuprizone to mimic multiple sclerosis, crocin from saffron improved movement and mood tests and raised antioxidant levels.

35917044.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes S1P1 signaling in demyelination
35917044.conclusion_quote: Our findings reveal β-arrestin-dependent S1P 1 signaling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells implying a role of S1P 1 signaling in remyelination.
35917044.summary: In mice given cuprizone to cause demyelination, researchers used glowing reporter mice to track where S1P1 receptor signaling occurs in brain cells during myelin damage and repair.

36966345.mechanism: Deleting NOS2 removes protective nitric oxide-driven immune control
36966345.conclusion_quote: Thus, our observations highlight a protective role of NOS2 in murine-β-coronavirus induced demyelination.
36966345.summary: In mice infected with a coronavirus that causes brain inflammation and myelin loss, removing the NOS2 gene led to stronger inflammation, earlier myelin damage, and lower survival.

37026017.conclusion_quote: Together, the results of our study revealed that the immediate ADRs induced by SMI were mediated by thymus-derived T cells, and elucidated the mechanisms of such ADRs.
37026017.summary: In mice, drug reactions caused by ShenMai injection depended on thymus-derived T cells. The study does not address multiple sclerosis.

36608690.mechanism: Chemokine boosts OPC proliferation and differentiation, calms microglia
36608690.conclusion_quote: Our results demonstrate a novel pro-regenerative role of fractalkine in a demyelinating mouse model.
36608690.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, infusing fractalkine into the brain increased new oligodendrocytes and improved myelin repair.

36204851.mechanism: Blocks fibronectin's inhibition, activates Erk1/2 and PI3K pathways
36204851.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest that poly-L-ornithine has the potential to be a treatment option for clinical myelin sheath injury.
36204851.summary: In cell cultures and mice with lysolecithin-induced focal demyelination, poly-L-ornithine blocked fibronectin's inhibition of oligodendrocyte maturation and improved myelin repair and motor recovery.

37813042.mechanism: Blocks SUMO, boosts myelin genes, cuts Th17 cells
37813042.conclusion_quote: The dual effects of deSUMOylation on remyelination and in regulating an autoimmune adaptive response offers a novel approach to the management of human inflammatory demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis.
37813042.summary: In mouse cell cultures and mice, the drug TAK981 blocked SUMO attachment, increased myelin repair after cuprizone damage, and reduced inflammation and disease severity in EAE mice.

36625077.mechanism: TREM2 loss impairs microglial myelin debris clearance
36625077.conclusion_quote: Together, we highlight the central role of TREM2 signaling in remyelination and neuroprotection.
36625077.summary: In mice with brain demyelination caused by lysolecithin, removing the TREM2 gene left myelin damage lasting weeks, caused nerve loss and impaired microglia clearing myelin debris.

37570807.mechanism: boosts oligodendrocyte precursor cell growth and maturation into myelin-forming
37570807.conclusion_quote: The multiple effects of icaritin make it a promising lead compound for remyelination therapy.
37570807.summary: In cell cultures and in mice given cuprizone to strip myelin, the plant compound icaritin boosted precursor cell growth and maturation, improved behavior, and increased myelin formation.

37904733.mechanism: activates AMPK energy sensor, shifts cell metabolism
37904733.conclusion_quote: In summary, metformin dramatically alters metabolism and accelerates oligodendroglial differentiation both in health and following myelin damage.
37904733.summary: In young mice with cuprizone-induced myelin damage, metformin sped early myelin repair and helped oligodendrocyte precursor cells mature into myelin-producing cells.

37429715.mechanism: Not applicable, describes disease model only
37429715.conclusion_quote: Retinal atrophy determined by GCC thickness (OCT) and RGC counts correlating with mobility impairment in the chronic phase of MOG-IgG and AQP4-IgG EAE may serve as a generalizable marker of neurodegeneration.
37429715.summary: In mice with EAE, antibodies against MOG or AQP4 caused visual decline and retinal nerve cell loss that tracked with worsening mobility, suggesting a possible marker of nerve damage.

37089039.mechanism: Not applicable, analytical chemistry method only
37089039.conclusion_quote: The method developed was found to be effective in estimating the amounts of Cu 2+ and furfural in cachaça samples, with a mean absolute error of 0.2 mg L -1 for the Cu 2+ model, and 0.3 mg per 100 mL of anhydrous alcohol for the furfural model.
37089039.summary: This chemistry study uses smartphone photos of color tests to measure copper and furfural in cachaça, a Brazilian spirit, and has no multiple sclerosis model.

37378418.mechanism: Not applicable: imaging method, not a treatment
37378418.conclusion_quote: Synthetic data generated by a physical model of contrast enhancement provided effective training for a deep learning model for contrast amplification.
37378418.summary: Researchers trained an AI to boost MRI contrast using simulated data, tested in rats with brain tumors and in patient scans that included some people with MS, not in an MS disease model.

36519759.conclusion_quote: Given the potent inflammatory response here identified in Krabbe disease and the other neurodegenerative disorders studied, a broad induction of inflammasomes is likely to be a dominant factor in the pathogenesis, and thus represents a platform for therapeutic exploration.
36519759.summary: In twitcher mice, a model of Krabbe disease that damages myelin, inflammation genes and proteins were found to rise as disease progressed.

38022591.conclusion_quote: Considering BTK expression in MS lesions and resident cells, BTKi may exert effect on B cells, microglia/macrophages in active lesions, and limit microglia activation in chronic active lesions, where tissue damage propagates.
38022591.summary: In postmortem MS brain tissue and in mice fed the toxin cuprizone, researchers measured Bruton's tyrosine kinase, finding higher levels in active and chronic active lesions and in microglia.

37267677.conclusion_quote: For the first time, our study revealed the common neuroinflammatory pathway in animal models of MS and introduced candidate hub genes for better evaluating the preclinical efficacy of pharmacological interventions and designing prospective targeted therapies.
37267677.summary: Researchers analyzed public gene data from mice with EAE and cuprizone models, finding shared inflammatory signals like TNF alpha, STAT1 and CXCL10 raised in blood serum.

36343678.mechanism: Antibody clears toxic cis-phosphorylated tau from neurons
36343678.conclusion_quote: Our results highlight the opportunity of using cis mAb as a new therapy for protecting myelin and axons in patients suffering from MS.
36343678.summary: In mice with chemically induced demyelination of the optic pathway, an antibody that clears toxic tau protected myelin and axons and improved vision.

38062768.conclusion_quote: These results indicate that CHI3L1 is associated with neuronal deterioration, pre-lesion pathology, along with inflammation in MS.
38062768.summary: Researchers examined CHI3L1 protein in brain tissue from people with multiple sclerosis and in mice fed cuprizone, finding it linked to neuron damage and inflammation.

36537341.conclusion_quote: These differences in the response to demyelination suggest that both volume dependent and species-specific mechanisms are critical in the regulation of OPC proliferation and lesion repopulation and suggest that alternate models will be necessary to fully understand the mechanisms that contribute to failed remyelination in MS.
36537341.summary: In rabbits with chronic lab-induced demyelination, myelin-producing progenitor cells failed to refill lesions, suggesting lesion size and species differences matter.

37426806.mechanism: kills protozoan parasites in laboratory tests
37426806.conclusion_quote: Compound 18 showed the highest antiplasmodial activity (IC 50 = 0.2 µm) and compound 24 inhibited T. b. rhodesiense with an IC 50 value of 0.007 µ M.
37426806.summary: Tested plant extracts and their compounds from Niger against parasites in lab dishes, finding some killed malaria and sleeping sickness parasites but were also toxic to rat muscle cells.

36762864.conclusion_quote: This finding provides a novel structural insight into the thermostability of sPLA 2 and could be applied to create mutant proteins with enhanced industrial potential.
36762864.summary: This study examined a heat-stable bacterial enzyme for industrial use and found it stays active at 50°C, but it does not involve multiple sclerosis or any MS model.

37312698.mechanism: Boosts antioxidant enzymes and reduces lipid peroxidation
37312698.conclusion_quote: These results suggested L-theanine has a protective effect against CPZ-induced MS in mice.
37312698.summary: In mice fed a cuprizone diet to mimic MS, theanine improved movement and balance and raised blood antioxidant levels.

36779010.mechanism: Blocks OPC differentiation, freeing neural stem cell remyelination
36779010.conclusion_quote: These results strongly suggest that pOPCs and NSC-progeny compete to repair white matter lesions.
36779010.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, blocking oligodendrocyte progenitor maturation let neural stem cell-derived cells move into damaged white matter and form more myelin-producing cells.

36769167.conclusion_quote: Overall, these findings demonstrate the predictive/prognostic value of quantitative and objective pre-infection DigiGait measurements for viral-induced neuromuscular dysfunction.
36769167.summary: In Collaborative Cross mice infected with a demyelinating virus, gait measured before infection predicted later neurological decline, suggesting gait tests may forecast later nerve dysfunction.

38935935.mechanism: Not applicable, computational analysis of existing gene data only
38935935.conclusion_quote: This study identified hitherto unexplored possible associations between Th9 and disease states.
38935935.summary: A computer analysis of public mouse gene data looked at genes that turn Th2 cells into Th9 cells, linking them to many diseases.

36557903.mechanism: reduces T-cell IL-17 and IFN-γ, macrophage NO and IL-6
36557903.conclusion_quote: Thus, PEGA is a potent anti-inflammatory compound with a perspective to be further explored in the context of CNS autoimmunity and other chronic inflammatory disorders.
36557903.summary: In an animal model of MS called EAE, a modified gallic acid compound named PEGA reduced harmful immune cell activity and inflammation and improved disease.

36291646.mechanism: Augments cholesterol transport and recycling to support myelin repair
36291646.conclusion_quote: Interventions to improve cholesterol homeostasis may be a viable approach to promoting the rehabilitation of MS patients.
36291646.summary: Gentisic acid, a compound that boosts cholesterol transport, improved movement, vision and nerve insulation in mice with EAE optic neuritis.

35753791.conclusion_quote: In the current article, the history of MS treatment and its future prospects will be reviewed and discussed.
35753791.summary: This review article describes how multiple sclerosis treatments developed over about 30 years, from interferon beta to newer strategies based on findings from patients.

36083288.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes Ero1α changes
36083288.conclusion_quote: Therefore, Ero1α induction makes astrocytes vulnerable to oxidative stress in the MS and EAE pathologies.
36083288.summary: In mice with EAE and in human MS tissue, astrocytes showed higher Ero1α, an enzyme producing reactive oxygen species, suggesting these cells become vulnerable to oxidative stress.

36761918.mechanism: blocks nitric oxide modification of GAPDH protein
36761918.conclusion_quote: Our findings suggest that SNO-GAPDH contributes to neuroaxonal injury during neuroinflammation and identify CGP3466b as a candidate neuroprotective therapy in MS.
36761918.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the drug CGP3466b blocked harmful GAPDH changes, reducing nerve damage and disability without affecting the immune system.

36103823.mechanism: Reduces T cell activation, proliferation and Th1 differentiation
36103823.conclusion_quote: These findings reveal specificity in the host response to fiber sources and define a pathway of fiber-induced immunomodulation that protects against pathologic neuroinflammation.
36103823.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, a diet supplemented with guar gum fiber delayed disease and calmed brain inflammation by reducing harmful T cell activity.

35679759.mechanism: not applicable, no treatment or genetic change tested
35679759.conclusion_quote: The generation of disease-specific iPSC lines from multiple members of a single family will facilitate MS genetic and functional studies.
35679759.summary: Researchers created four human stem cell lines from family members with multiple sclerosis, providing cell models for future genetic and functional studies of the disease.

36209613.conclusion_quote: The results indicate that symptoms and progression of EAE can be reliably measured by VSOP as a non-motor function assessment.
36209613.summary: In mice with EAE, a simple urine test on paper tracked bladder problems that matched disease severity and was affected by transport stress.

36340004.conclusion_quote: RMSD, Rg, and RMSF analysis of an MD simulation trajectory indicate a stable and compact state throughout the simulation period of modeled proteins.
36340004.summary: Computer simulations modeled the structure of mouse grancalcin, a protein raised in mice with EAE, finding it stable and compact over 100 nanoseconds.

36029169.mechanism: Anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions prevent myelin loss
36029169.conclusion_quote: Treatment with ginger inhibited demyelination and alleviated remyelination of corpus callosum in rats.
36029169.summary: In rats with cuprizone-induced demyelination, the highest dose of ginger extract prevented loss of myelin in the corpus callosum.

35791633.mechanism: promotes oligodendrocyte progenitor maturation and remyelination
35791633.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest that remyelinating actions of LKE can potentially be formulated to induce remyelination in neurological diseases associated with demyelination including MS.
35791633.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, lanthionine ketenamine ethyl ester increased myelin thickness and mature oligodendrocytes, improving remyelination.

36327618.mechanism: Inhibits ferroptosis, reducing lipid peroxidation and iron-driven oligodendrocyt
36327618.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these findings demonstrate that OL loss and demyelination may be induced in EAE through, at least in part, a mechanism of ferroptosis.
36327618.summary: In mice with EAE, a ferroptosis inhibitor called Fer-1 largely reversed oligodendrocyte death and demyelination, suggesting ferroptosis contributes to myelin loss.

36288210.mechanism: Boosts microglial myelin clearance through NRF2 and RUBCN
36288210.conclusion_quote: Together, this study proves that NNVs can modulate neuroinflammation by clearing myelin debris and is a promising MS treatment strategy.
36288210.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, nanovesicles made from neutrophils helped microglia clear myelin debris, which reduced inflammation and improved nerve function and white matter.

36253847.mechanism: Promotes gut bacteria that induce regulatory T cells
36253847.conclusion_quote: We identified vancomycin as a potent modulator of the gut-brain axis by promoting the proliferation of bacterial species that induce regulatory T cells.
36253847.summary: In mice with EAE, the antibiotic vancomycin and the gut bacterium Anaerotruncus colihominis both reduced disease, linked to more regulatory T cells.

35585921.mechanism: promotes oligodendrocyte maturation and myelin repair
35585921.conclusion_quote: Diet supplementation with Acer truncatum oil attenuates demyelination induced by cuprizone, indicating that Acer truncatum oil is a novel therapeutic diet in demyelinating diseases.
35585921.summary: In mice given cuprizone to damage myelin, a diet with Acer truncatum oil after withdrawal boosted myelin repair and eased schizophrenia like behavior.

35226368.conclusion_quote: Our findings recapitulate several disease features described in patients and provide new mechanistic insights into the metabolic rewiring of astrocytes in MS, which could be targeted in future therapeutic studies.
35226368.summary: Researchers grew astrocyte cells from stem cells of people with multiple sclerosis and healthy controls, finding altered mitochondria, glutamate handling, and metabolism that mirror the disease.

35334928.mechanism: Restores gut microbiota balance and reduces nerve damage
35334928.conclusion_quote: Finally, the present study demonstrated that VBC treatment ameliorated the cellular changes in the affected peripheral nerve, muscles innervated by this nerve, and the gut microbiota dysbiosis which occurred during the EAE.
35334928.summary: In rats with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, vitamin B complex eased symptoms, sped recovery, and improved the balance of gut bacteria.

35568723.mechanism: Suppressing ETS1 triggers endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, weakening the b
35568723.conclusion_quote: Together, these results demonstrate a functional role of EndMT in blood-brain barrier dysfunction and propose ETS1 as a potential transcriptional switch of EndMT to target the development of multiple sclerosis.
35568723.summary: Researchers found that suppressing the gene ETS1 in blood vessel cells of the brain worsened barrier leakage and fibrosis in mice with EAE, a model of MS.

36430480.conclusion_quote: We identify genes deregulated during a restricted time frame, and we provide insight into the timing and interrelationships of pathological disease processes at the organ and cell levels.
36430480.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, researchers mapped gene activity changes in the brain, spinal cord, microglia and oligodendrocyte cells across disease stages.

36026478.mechanism: cathelicidin potentiates Th17 differentiation and T cell activation
36026478.conclusion_quote: We propose that cathelicidin exposure results in highly activated, cytokine-producing T cells, which drive autoimmunity; this is a mechanism through which neutrophils amplify inflammation in the central nervous system.
36026478.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, those lacking the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin had much milder disease because cathelicidin helps immune cells that attack the nervous system.

35709748.mechanism: not applicable, describes disease mechanism only
35709748.conclusion_quote: Our study suggests that targeting the bone marrow niche presents an avenue to treat MS and other autoimmune disorders.
35709748.summary: In MS patients and mice with EAE, bone marrow stem cells shift toward making myeloid immune cells as T cells gather there, which feeds brain inflammation.

36153399.mechanism: Lowers kynurenine pathway enzymes, AhR, and Nnmt, raises NAD+
36153399.conclusion_quote: Collectively, this study suggests that MT treatment may significantly attenuates the severity of EAE by altering the KP, AhR and NAD + metabolism.
36153399.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, melatonin treatment reduced disease severity and plaques by altering kynurenine pathway, AhR and NAD+ metabolism.

35868535.conclusion_quote: The observed discrepancies can result from a complex network of interactions between inflammation and fibrosis, as well as between liver cells and the extracellular matrix influencing the biomechanical properties of the liver tissue.
35868535.summary: In mice with EAE, natalizumab reduced liver inflammation but had mixed effects on liver stiffness depending on disease stage.

36050813.mechanism: Raises cytokines and lowers regulatory T cell share
36050813.conclusion_quote: Altogether, our results demonstrate that infection of mice with T. canis worsens the course of subsequently induced EAE.
36050813.summary: In mice with EAE, prior infection with the dog roundworm Toxocara canis made disease worse, with more weight loss, higher clinical scores, and raised cytokines.

35489221.mechanism: inhibits Wnt3a/β-catenin signaling, promotes oligodendrocyte maturation
35489221.conclusion_quote: Taken together, these findings indicate that MAT treatment promoted the maturation of OLs and myelin repair, which is closely related to the modulation of the Wnt/β-catenin/TCF7L2 signaling pathway.
35489221.summary: In mice with EAE, matrine reduced Wnt signaling and helped oligodendrocytes mature and rebuild myelin, suggesting a repair benefit.

35615905.mechanism: Reduces pathogenic peripheral Treg cells, restoring Treg/Teff balance
35615905.conclusion_quote: These results provide evidence and mechanism that accumulated aged pTreg cells play a detrimental role in neuronal inflammation of aged MS.
35615905.summary: In aged mice with EAE, inhibiting FoxP3 or depleting peripheral regulatory T cells partially restored immune balance in the brain and spinal cord and reduced disease.

36470947.mechanism: Describes sex differences in sensory neuron responses
36470947.conclusion_quote: Our results demonstrate that male sensory neurons are more sensitive to mitochondrial stress, making them prone to neuronal injury.
36470947.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, male and female pain sensing nerve cells responded differently to inflammation, and male cells were more prone to injury.

35366992.conclusion_quote: Most importantly, all models of EAE utilize myelin-reactive T cells to target the myelin sheath, which allows for the effective investigation and testing of immunomodulatory therapies for MS.
35366992.summary: This methods chapter describes how to induce, observe, score and measure experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, an animal model of MS, in laboratory animals.

36710925.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our findings confirm a regionalized distribution of inflammation in the hippocampus of EAE-mice.
36710925.summary: In SJL/J mice with EAE, a model of MS, inflammation in the hippocampus was concentrated in certain regions, with altered splicing of the Arhgef9 gene in those same areas.

35325396.mechanism: Enhances MSC suppression of T-cell proliferation
35325396.conclusion_quote: Our targeted transplantation procedure of modified MSC can be applied to improve the effectiveness of cellular therapy for multiple sclerosis and other autoimmune disorders.
35325396.summary: In mice with EAE, stem cells engineered to carry an IL-23 receptor construct reduced inflammation and improved myelin better than regular stem cells.

35835801.conclusion_quote: Our findings stress the needs for both high b-values and sufficient NDIR to achieve a GM DTI with more biologically meaningful correlations, though DTI-metrics should be interpreted with caution in these settings.
35835801.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, high b-value diffusion MRI scans detected early hippocampal changes that standard scans missed.

35061807.conclusion_quote: Our approach was sufficient to develop a demyelinating lesion with high reproducibility and low morbidity.
35061807.summary: Researchers built a rat model of multiple sclerosis by immunizing rats and injecting a protein into the brain to create demyelinating lesions in a chosen location.

35716476.mechanism: reduces inflammation and demyelination in EAE
35716476.conclusion_quote: It could be concluded that V. odorata is a rich source of cyclotides which they could be extracted by an easily available process and also, they could be used as immunomodulatory agents in MS, with similar effects to fingolimod.
35716476.summary: Cyclotide fractions from the plant Viola odorata were given to mice with EAE, a model of MS, reducing clinical symptoms, inflammation and demyelination, similar to fingolimod.

37283612.mechanism: delivers myelin antigen to M cells, inducing tolerance
37283612.conclusion_quote: These results demonstrate the practicality of soybean as a host for producing and formulating immune-modulating therapies to treat autoimmune diseases.
37283612.summary: Oral soymilk containing a myelin protein made in soybeans and fused to a reovirus protein delayed and reduced disease in mice with EAE, a model of MS.

36243931.mechanism: upregulates GATA3 and miR-27-3p isoform expression
36243931.conclusion_quote: The protective impacts of vitamins A and D in EAE mice may be mediated by the upregulation of GATA3.
36243931.summary: In mice with EAE, vitamins A and D, alone or combined and given before disease induction, raised GATA3 and miR-27-3p levels, suggesting a protective immune effect.

34988943.conclusion_quote: Here we describe the detailed protocol for establishing iPSCs from peripheral blood mononuclear cells that we have utilized to model multiple sclerosis.
34988943.summary: This protocol paper describes how to create stem cells from blood cells of people with multiple sclerosis, using a method that avoids leaving foreign genetic material behind.

35380252.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes markers only
35380252.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our results acknowledged that GFAP, vimentin, LCN2, and ALDH1L1 serve as reliable marker to identify activated astrocytes during cuprizone-induced de- and remyelination.
35380252.summary: In mice given the toxin cuprizone, researchers compared astrocyte marker proteins during myelin loss and repair, finding GFAP, vimentin, LCN2 and ALDH1L1 reliably identify activated astrocytes.

36499161.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes gene expression changes
36499161.conclusion_quote: This study characterized the transcriptome pattern in the hippocampi of mice with EAE and signaling pathways underpinning hippocampal dysfunction.
36499161.summary: In mice with EAE, RNA sequencing found 1202 differentially expressed hippocampal genes, with immune genes up and synaptic and memory genes down.

36164343.mechanism: High-fat diet alters gut bacteria, increases gut permeability
36164343.conclusion_quote: This study provides evidence for the involvement of the gut microbiome and associated metabolic pathways plus gut permeability in obesity-induced modulation of EAE disease severity.
36164343.summary: In HLA-DR3 transgenic mice with EAE, a high-fat diet caused obesity, gut bacterial imbalance and leaky gut, which made the disease more severe.

33863858.conclusion_quote: Our data indicate that activated microglia within the central amygdala may contribute to the sexually dimorphic effects of morphine and may drive neuronal adaptations that lead to pain hypersensitivity in EAE.
33863858.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, activated immune cells called microglia in the amygdala were linked to pain sensitivity and weaker morphine pain relief.

37093915.conclusion_quote: Our study demonstrates that leukocyte migration in an MS model is distinctly different from the control, suggesting that leukocytes may play a key role in the development of retinal vascular inflammation and optic neuritis during MS, warranting further investigation of the pathological roles of leukocytes in the disease onset and progression.
37093915.summary: Researchers used glowing green cells and a live eye scanner to track immune cell movement in the retina of mice with EAE, finding more immune cells sticking to blood vessels.

35580468.conclusion_quote: Considering its high reproducibility and inter-rater reliability, "I AM D EAE" is a useful tool for EAE monitoring.
35580468.summary: A new scoring tool called I AM D EAE was tested in mice with EAE and proved reproducible, closely matching the standard five level scale used to monitor disease.

35135958.mechanism: Loss reduces antigen presentation and inflammatory cytokine expression
35135958.conclusion_quote: These observations suggest a novel function of Clec1A in the immune system.
35135958.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, removing the Clec1a gene produced milder disease with less spinal cord inflammation and reduced inflammatory cytokines.

35553640.mechanism: blocks NF-κB signaling, reducing NLRP3 inflammasome activation
35553640.conclusion_quote: BAY11-7082 is a promising therapeutic agent for MS.
35553640.summary: In mice with EAE, a drug blocking NF-κB lowered NLRP3 inflammasome levels and improved clinical scores whether given before or after symptoms began.

36120103.mechanism: not applicable, describes disease biology only
36120103.conclusion_quote: Thus, based on our data, we propose a negative regulation of autophagy in MS, possibly through persistent mTORC1 activation, which depends on the lesion stage.
36120103.summary: In mice with EAE and in human MS brain tissue, genes that drive autophagy were less active, especially in lesion cores, while mTORC1 signaling was overactive.

35961059.mechanism: Lowers inflammatory cytokines and raises antioxidant enzyme expression
35961059.conclusion_quote: Overall, our results suggest that IM253 could ameliorate the severity of EAE, probably because of its anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties, and support the preclinical effects of IM253 as a potential therapeutic intervention.
35961059.summary: In mice with EAE, a herbal compound called IM253 lowered brain inflammation and demyelination while boosting antioxidant defenses.

35085379.mechanism: activates Wnt/β-catenin signalling to strengthen barrier and reduce inflammation
35085379.conclusion_quote: Our study provides evidence for an intrinsic impairment of BBB function in MS patients that can be modelled in vitro.
35085379.summary: Blood-brain barrier cells made from stem cells of MS patients showed weaker barriers and more inflammation, and turning on Wnt signalling partly improved them.

36210424.mechanism: none, describes disease without a treatment
36210424.conclusion_quote: The development of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis is accompanied by degradation and death of neurons, in particular ChAT + motor neurons.
36210424.summary: In mice with EAE, a multiple sclerosis model, spinal cord motor neurons were lost, with large empty areas forming in chronic disease.

34757579.mechanism: Modulates inflammasome, IDO and cytokine gene expression
34757579.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our study provides insight into how the therapeutic effect of the chosen strain of probiotic was correlated with the modulation of the level of inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines.
34757579.summary: In mice given cuprizone to cause demyelination, a probiotic lowered inflammation and improved myelin repair and maze performance.

35410627.mechanism: Reduces Th1/Th17 responses and dendritic cell co-stimulation
35410627.conclusion_quote: Our data demonstrate that the readily available MB-MSCs significantly reduced the disease severity of EAE upon transplantation.
35410627.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, transplanted stem cells from menstrual blood reduced disease severity by calming harmful immune T cells and dendritic cells.

35843021.conclusion_quote: Established hiPSCs are a valuable source for studies of MS disease modeling and drug discovery.
35843021.summary: Researchers turned blood immune cells from one person with multiple sclerosis into stem cells that can become many cell types, creating a reusable lab resource for studying the disease.

35064931.mechanism: Blocks ANXA2 signaling at the blood-brain barrier
35064931.conclusion_quote: In summary, the activation of ANXA2 signaling at the BBB appear to play an important role in the pathogenesis of EAE.
35064931.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, daily treatment with a peptide that blocks the ANXA2 protein suppressed disease development, pointing to blood-brain barrier involvement.

35392156.mechanism: Environmental exposure only, no treatment tested
35392156.conclusion_quote: Although the mouse EAE model does not fully recapitulate the pathology or symptoms of MS in humans, these findings largely corroborate previous epidemiological findings that exposure to CS can worsen the symptoms and pathology of MS.
35392156.summary: In mice with EAE, low and medium doses of cigarette smoke worsened symptoms and spinal cord damage, while the high dose had no effect.

36004706.mechanism: Mushroom biological response modifiers suppress demyelination
36004706.conclusion_quote: The four medicinal mushrooms may be promising BRMs for prevention and alleviation of the symptoms of MS.
36004706.summary: In cuprizone-fed mice modeling MS, diets containing certain medicinal mushrooms reduced myelin loss, and some improved motor coordination on a rotarod test.

35750335.mechanism: Expands regulatory T cells suppressing pathogenic CD4 cells
35750335.conclusion_quote: Our results demonstrated that the therapeutic effect of U.S. Food and Drug Administration-approved anti-CD52 mAb is dependent on the presence of Tregs.
35750335.summary: In mice with EAE and in blood cells from people with MS, anti-CD52 antibody treatment expanded regulatory T cells, and its benefit depended on those cells being present.

36482934.mechanism: activates Cdc42/Rac1 signaling to promote oligodendrocyte differentiation
36482934.conclusion_quote: Overall, our study is the first to reveal that catalpol can promote OL generation and myelination and contributes to the crucial regulatory process of GEF-Cdc42/Rac1 signaling expression and activation.
36482934.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the natural compound catalpol promoted oligodendrocyte formation and myelin repair, while reducing neurological symptoms and inflammation.

36161894.mechanism: Activates S1PR5 on oligodendrocytes, protecting them from degeneration
36161894.conclusion_quote: Our study demonstrates that siponimod exerts protective effects in the brain in a S1PR5-dependent manner.
36161894.summary: In mice fed the toxin cuprizone, siponimod protected myelin producing cells and nerve fibres, but this protection disappeared in mice lacking the S1PR5 receptor.

35406658.mechanism: Drives fibroblasts into oligodendrocyte-like cells that rescue myelin
35406658.conclusion_quote: These results provide a foundation for exploring the development of a treatment for demyelinating diseases via regenerative medicine.
35406658.summary: In mice with cuprizone-induced demyelination, injecting three small molecules directly into the brain rescued myelin loss within two weeks.

35451371.mechanism: Gene deletion blocks AIM2 inflammasome activation in astrocytes
35451371.conclusion_quote: Thus, the AIM2 inflammasome activation in astrocytes may have a distinct role from traditional inflammasome-mediated inflammation.
35451371.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the AIM2 gene prevented inflammasome activation in astrocytes, which were most active after the disease peak, suggesting an unusual role for this pathway.

34920025.mechanism: Not applicable, describes EAE induction protocol
34920025.conclusion_quote: Higher standards for comparability and reproducibility are needed to ensure and maximize the generation of reliable EAE data.
34920025.summary: In mice with EAE, the researchers found that the pertussis toxin dose must be adjusted to its batch potency to produce consistent disease, reducing the number of mice needed.

35408977.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that TRPV2 may be a key player in myelination in accordance with the recapitulation hypothesis, and that it may become an interesting clinical target in the treatment of demyelination disorders.
35408977.summary: Researchers measured TRPV2 levels in mice with jimpy hypomyelination, cuprizone and EAE demyelination models, and in MS patient samples, finding it rises with remyelination and inflammation.

35448617.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, systemic infections by non- albicans Candida strains exerted influence on the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis in both immunological and clinical aspects, emphasizing their possible relevance in MS development.
35448617.summary: In mice with EAE, infection by C. glabrata or C. krusei worsened paralysis and immune responses, while C. parapsilosis did not affect disease severity.

35958570.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes complement activation in disease
35958570.conclusion_quote: Overall, these results indicate potential divergent roles for the complement system in MS.
35958570.summary: In mice with two MS-like diseases, one relapsing and one progressive, complement immune proteins rose in the spinal cord and appeared to play different roles.

35762739.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our study implicates oxidative stress in ODC mitochondria as a novel pre-clinical sign of MS-like inflammation and demonstrates that evolving redox and morphological changes in mitochondria accompany ODC dysfunction during neuroinflammation.
35762739.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, oligodendrocyte mitochondria became oxidized early, before immune cells entered the spinal cord, and their shape and density became altered.

36499143.conclusion_quote: Together this constitutes a toolkit for 3-dimensional immunostaining to monitor general optic nerve pathology and fast automated quantification of axonal defects that could also be adapted to monitor axonal degeneration and inflammation in other neurodegenerative disease models.
36499143.summary: Researchers developed a 3D staining method and an AI tool to measure inflammation and axon damage in the optic nerve of mice with EAE.

35908626.mechanism: Inactivates AXL/JAK2/STAT3 pathway, reducing microglia-mediated inflammation
35908626.conclusion_quote: The findings clarify that curcumin may inhibit the inflammatory response mediated by microglia by inactivating the AXL/JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway, which laid a theoretical foundation for the clinical management of MS.
35908626.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, curcumin reduced disease severity and calmed microglia, the brain's immune cells, by blocking the AXL/JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway.

35597080.conclusion_quote: Observed changes validate the use of W5 and W7 temporal moments for the study of demyelination and early remyelination in this model.
35597080.summary: In male mice fed cuprizone, myelin protein dropped after five weeks and recovered by seven weeks, validating this timeline for studying early remyelination.

35354603.mechanism: Modulates S1P receptors, reduces inflammation and promotes promyelinating microg
35354603.conclusion_quote: These results confirm the immunomodulatory effects of siponimod and suggest additional regenerative and promyelinating effects, which follow the dynamics of a bell-shaped curve with high being less efficient than low concentrations.
35354603.summary: Siponimod helped myelin repair in mice and tadpoles and reduced optic nerve inflammation and vision loss in EAE mice, with lower doses working best.

35856297.mechanism: Lcn2 deletion removes secreted inflammatory modulator
35856297.conclusion_quote: Together, our results highlight LCN2 as a potentially protective molecule in MS lesion formation, which might be able to limit loss of oligodendrocytes immune-cell invasion.
35856297.summary: In mice with cuprizone, EAE, and combined models, removing the Lcn2 gene increased oligodendrocyte loss and immune cell invasion in the brain, suggesting LCN2 protects against MS lesions.

35863299.mechanism: Blocks lymphocyte exit, protecting spinal cord motor circuits
35863299.conclusion_quote: These findings suggest that fingolimod preserves gait in RRMS patients by protecting motor circuits in the spinal cord.
35863299.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, daily oral fingolimod started after symptoms began improved walking and reduced spinal cord damage.

34181005.conclusion_quote: As MS most often develops in young to middle-aged people, this new tool may have significant value for use in EAE animal studies as a first step toward translation to people with MS.
34181005.summary: Researchers adapted a frailty index for mice with EAE, a model of MS, and found it captured more health problems across ages than the standard paralysis scale.

35219910.mechanism: Blocks CCR1, suppressing Th9 and Th22 cell markers
35219910.conclusion_quote: These results confirmed that J-113863 suppressed Th9/Th22 cells to reduce demyelination in EAE mice, suggesting its potential role as a novel drug candidate for MS treatment.
35219910.summary: A CCR1 blocking drug, J-113863, reduced disease severity in mice with EAE, an MS model, by lowering immune cells that drive inflammation.

36348455.mechanism: Interferes with DNA synthesis, depleting dividing lymphocytes
36348455.conclusion_quote: Our results indicate that cladribine exerts a neuroprotective effect after crossing the blood-brain barrier independently of its peripheral immunosuppressant action.
36348455.summary: In mice with EAE, an MS model, oral cladribine reduced clinical deficits and partly restored brain circuit activity in the auditory cortex, with effects that were temporary.

34976589.mechanism: Blocks microglial GCPII enzyme, raising brain NAAG levels
34976589.conclusion_quote: These data support further development of D-2PMPA to attenuate elevated microglial GCPII activity and treat cognitive impairment in MS.
34976589.summary: In mice with EAE, a dendrimer carrier delivering a drug to activated microglia improved memory on a maze without changing physical symptoms.

36343517.conclusion_quote: Thus, high K + intake attenuates EAE, possibly by increasing the Treg cells.
36343517.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of multiple sclerosis, a high potassium diet delayed and reduced disease and increased regulatory T cells.

36246526.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes intrinsic oligodendrocyte gene changes
36246526.conclusion_quote: Altogether, our findings suggest that mature OLs in PPMS affected individuals carry intrinsic abnormalities that could contribute, at least in part, to the pathophysiology of this form of the disease.
36246526.summary: Researchers grew brain cells called oligodendrocytes from stem cells of people with primary progressive MS and healthy people, finding many altered genes, including higher NLRP2.

35197067.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes disease only
35197067.conclusion_quote: Therefore, by documenting visual changes induced by bMOG and showing similarities to those seen in diseases such as multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica, this study offers a new approach to test protective or restorative ophthalmic treatments.
35197067.summary: In mice with EAE induced by bMOG, visual acuity stayed impaired after motor function partly recovered, linked to retinal inflammation and gliosis.

35180820.mechanism: Treadmill exercise improves memory and adrenal gland morphology
35180820.conclusion_quote: The experimental design selected for this study appears to be an effective treatment for memory in rats with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
35180820.summary: Rats with EAE, a model of MS, that exercised on a treadmill before and after disease induction performed better on a maze memory test than untreated EAE rats.

35126713.mechanism: Restores myelination in cortical areas via neuromodulation
35126713.conclusion_quote: Therefore, the results of the present study indicated that LFMS may be a promising therapy for demyelinating diseases due to the improvement of depressive symptoms via regulation of myelination in cortical areas.
35126713.summary: In female mice fed a cuprizone diet to cause demyelination, low-field magnetic stimulation reduced depression-like behavior and reduced myelin loss in the prefrontal cortex.

35145527.summary: This is a correction notice for an earlier study on ultrasound lesions in mice, and it reports no new experimental findings.

35488271.conclusion_quote: These results highlight c-Met as an immune marker of highly pathogenic pro-inflammatory and pro-migratory CD4 + T lymphocytes associated with neuroinflammation.
35488271.summary: In mice with EAE, an MS model, immune T cells carrying the MET receptor and integrin alpha4 were more inflammatory and harmful, and also appeared in MS patients.

35043454.conclusion_quote: Increasing MOG dosage augmented visual function impairment in EAE, which could be monitored with VEP recording to assess demyelination and axonal loss along ONs.
35043454.summary: In female rats with EAE, higher doses of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein caused greater visual impairment and optic nerve damage, measurable with visual evoked potential recordings.

34823122.conclusion_quote: This method should impact MS research by making histological comparisons of EAE increasingly robust.
34823122.summary: This study describes a digital imaging method that measures inflammation, nerve loss, and myelin across the whole spinal cord of mice with EAE, a model of MS.

35872534.mechanism: Blocks CCR5, lowering inflammatory cytokines and transcription factors
35872534.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our data demonstrated that DAPTA could ameliorate EAE progression through the downregulation of the inflammation-related cytokines and transcription factors signaling, which may be useful for the clinical therapy of MS.
35872534.summary: In mice with EAE, a drug called DAPTA that blocks the CCR5 immune receptor reduced disease severity and lowered inflammatory signals in the brain.

35326455.mechanism: inhibits Th17 development via reduced dendritic cell IL-6
35326455.conclusion_quote: Our findings revealed that AD and EAE could coexist in the same mouse, and Aβ residing in peripheral circulation likely plays an anti-inflammatory role in preventing EAE progression.
35326455.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, injecting the amyloid beta 42 peptide reduced disease symptoms and blocked inflammatory Th17 immune cell development.

36155395.mechanism: Not applicable, describes disease model only
36155395.conclusion_quote: To avoid the shortcomings of a single intervention, new indicators to assess EAE based on clinical manifestations of anxiety-like moods and osteoporosis in MS patients are created to provide a more comprehensive assessment of MS treatment.
36155395.summary: This protocol paper explains how to induce EAE in mice with MOG35-55 and new ways to score disease, including mood changes and bone loss.

35252186.mechanism: Covalently binds NLRP3, blocking NEK7 interaction
35252186.conclusion_quote: Thus, our results identify manoalide as a selective and covalent NLRP3 inhibitor and suggest it has the potential for the treatment of NLRP3-associated diseases.
35252186.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, the small molecule manoalide blocked the NLRP3 inflammation switch and reduced disease severity.

35776890.mechanism: represses IL-17A production independently of YAP
35776890.conclusion_quote: The data suggest verteprofin's mode of action for the design of novel therapeutic autoimmune disease intervention.
35776890.summary: In mice with EAE, the drug verteporfin reduced inflammatory IL-17A production and eased disease, acting without its usual YAP target.

36571423.mechanism: Not applicable: describes emulsion preparation for EAE induction
36571423.conclusion_quote: It is simple and fast and uses a shaking homogenizer instead of syringes to prepare quality-controlled emulsions.
36571423.summary: This paper describes a quick, standardized method using a shaking homogenizer to prepare antigen and adjuvant emulsions for inducing EAE, an animal model of MS.

35417812.mechanism: Lower NFAT5 raises regulatory T cell frequency
35417812.conclusion_quote: We conclude that NFAT5 contributes to pathogenesis of EAE in female mice, possibly through decreasing tissue specific frequency of Treg cells.
35417812.summary: In female mice with EAE, reducing NFAT5 levels lessened disease severity and increased regulatory T cells, which help calm the immune system.

35461109.mechanism: Suppresses reactive A1 astrocytes and inflammation
35461109.conclusion_quote: These findings provide novel insights into the protective effect of MASM on EAE, which may be a promising drug candidate for treatment of EAE.
35461109.summary: In mice with EAE, a matrine derivative called MASM reduced harmful astrocyte activation, inflammation, demyelination and nerve loss, and improved blood-brain barrier function.

35276582.mechanism: Blocks immune cell migration and Th1/Th17 cell differentiation
35276582.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our work demonstrated that TPN10466 provided protection against the autoimmune disease EAE by inhibiting the migration of immune cells and suppressing Th1/Th17 differentiation, suggesting that TPN10466 could be a potential for promising potential agent for the treatment of MS/EAE.
35276582.summary: In experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), an artemisinin derivative called TPN10466 eased disease by blocking immune cell migration and Th1 and Th17 cell formation.

35906000.mechanism: Blocks gasdermin D pore formation and IL-1β release
35906000.conclusion_quote: Collectively, our findings provide a new molecule with the potential for translational application in GSDMD-associated inflammatory diseases.
35906000.summary: In mice with EAE and sepsis, the oral drug C202-2729 blocked gasdermin D, reducing inflammation and easing EAE severity comparably to teriflunomide.

35902536.mechanism: blocks IL-21 binding to its receptor
35902536.conclusion_quote: All these clinical results highlight the pleiotropicity of this cytokine in the different clinical stages and its key role in the EAE immunopathogenesis.
35902536.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, gene therapy blocking IL-21 signalling protected against disease when given early but was counterproductive during the immune response.

35205095.mechanism: Not applicable, observational study of brain stiffness
35205095.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, sexual dimorphism in the ECM composition of cortical tissue in the mouse brain is reflected by in vivo stiffness measured with MRE and should be considered in future studies by sex-specific reference values.
35205095.summary: Mice with EAE and healthy mice of both sexes showed sex differences in brain matrix gene expression and cortical stiffness measured by MRE.

35178050.conclusion_quote: Collectively, this study suggested that peripheral CCR6 + CXCR6 + CD4 T cells were Th17 cells with cytotoxic property in EAE model, and highlighted the cytotoxic granzymes for EAE pathology.
35178050.summary: In mice with EAE, researchers identified a subset of CD4 T cells marked by CCR6 and CXCR6 that is cytotoxic and produces granzymes, which may contribute to disease.

36552147.conclusion_quote: Therefore, this study provides a better understanding of the sex differences involved in the behavioural aspects of cuprizone-induced demyelination, which could allow for a better translation of results from the laboratory to the clinic.
36552147.summary: In male and female mice given cuprizone to cause demyelination, myelin damage was similar, but movement and anxiety deficits differed by sex.

35994513.mechanism: Reduces muscle mitochondrial damage and activates satellite cells
35994513.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, the attenuation of ultrastructural alterations in muscle fibers and activation response of satellite cells caused by EAE indicated that skeletal muscle had a regenerative response to TMS.
35994513.summary: In rats with EAE, transcranial magnetic stimulation reduced muscle fiber damage and activated muscle repair cells, suggesting a regenerative response in skeletal muscle.

35246882.conclusion_quote: In summary, this study demonstrates that TMEM119 is not exclusively expressed by microglia nor does it label all microglia, especially under cellular stress conditions.
35246882.summary: In mice with cuprizone, EAE, stroke and Parkinson disease models, and in MS brain tissue, the microglia marker TMEM119 decreased under stress, so it is not a reliable marker.

36241864.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes cuprizone-induced astrocyte changes
36241864.conclusion_quote: These findings indicate changes in BBB function that will have an impact on the milieu of the central nervous system (CNS) in the cuprizone model and need to be considered when studying the mechanisms of de- and remyelination.
36241864.summary: Using the cuprizone model of demyelination, researchers found swollen astrocyte endfeet and fluid buildup around brain blood vessels even at low cuprizone doses.

36466826.mechanism: Removing PINK1 alters peripheral immune cell responses
36466826.conclusion_quote: PINK1 plays an age-related role in modulating the peripheral inflammatory response during EAE, potentially contributing to the pathogenesis of neuroinflammatory and other associated conditions.
36466826.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting the PINK1 gene caused earlier onset and worse disease in adults, with more immune cells and inflammation, while younger mice had milder disease.

35766122.conclusion_quote: By combining mass spectrometry, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, computational chemistry, and other techniques, a self-consistent picture of the copper coordination structures of the blue and green complexes is revealed - confirming that the blue complex is in the Cu(III) state, containing two hydrolyzed cuprizone ligands per metal centre, while the green complex represents an extended oligomeric complex, comprised of repeating Cu(II) centres that lie 4.8 Å apart and are bridged by unhydrolyzed cuprizone donors.
35766122.summary: This chemistry study determined the structures of copper cuprizone complexes, a compound used to induce demyelination in mice, without testing any animals or treatments.

35994846.mechanism: Promotes OPC differentiation via GSK3β/β-Catenin pathway
35994846.conclusion_quote: By paving the way for OPCs differentiation, Rg1 could maintain the integrity of myelin and is a promising candidate for functional recovery in demyelinating diseases.
35994846.summary: In mice with a cuprizone model of demyelination and in EAE, the natural compound ginsenoside Rg1 helped precursor cells form new myelin and improved movement and memory.

36142395.mechanism: not applicable, no treatment or gene change tested
36142395.conclusion_quote: Together, these results provide a novel understanding about the influences of genetic variation on the acute neuropathological and immunopathological environment and viral load, which collectively lead to variable disease outcomes.
36142395.summary: In Collaborative Cross mice infected with Theiler's virus, brain viral load and inflammation varied by genetic background, with the hippocampus most affected.

35987252.mechanism: reduces TNF, IL-6, IL-17 and STAT3 activation
35987252.conclusion_quote: We reveal for the first time that AB4 protects against EAE by modulating inflammatory responses and the gut microbiota, demonstrating that AB4 may have potential as a therapeutic agent for treating MS in humans.
35987252.summary: Anemoside B4, a compound from a traditional Chinese herbal medicine, reduced disease severity, inflammation and demyelination in mice with EAE and reshaped their gut bacteria.

34826154.mechanism: depletes lymphocytes then alters innate immune cell activation
34826154.conclusion_quote: The findings of differential modulation of the microglia and infiltrating macrophages in the CNS in comparison with the innate immune cells in the peripheral organs support the CNS-specific beneficial effect of alemtuzumab treatment on inhibiting neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis patients.
34826154.summary: In mice with EAE, an anti-CD52 antibody changed immune cells in the blood and spleen differently than in the brain and spinal cord, reducing activation markers on brain immune cells.

35677535.conclusion_quote: These findings provide the first evidence of a sex-specific thermal response to immune-mediated demyelination, thus proposing a non-invasive assessment approach of the psychophysiological dynamics in EAE mice.
35677535.summary: Female mice with EAE, a mouse model of MS, got sicker, more fatigued and anxious than males and showed higher body temperatures.

35766818.conclusion_quote: Using density functional structure models and thermodynamic calculations we address several of the long-standing questions surrounding the copper-cuprizone reaction, as well as identify the likely reaction pathway that gives rise to the blue and green products.
35766818.summary: This chemistry study uses computer models to explain how copper reacts with cuprizone, a chemical used to induce demyelination in mice, but does not test MS.

36516268.mechanism: Variant boosts regulatory T cell suppressive capacity
36516268.conclusion_quote: Our data suggest that dysregulation of epigenetic modifiers, a distinct molecular class associated with disease risk, may influence disease onset.
36516268.summary: In mice with EAE, removing HDAC7 from regulatory T cells worsened disease, while a knock-in mouse carrying the protective human HDAC7 variant had milder disease.

35959804.mechanism: suppresses differentiation and activity of pathogenic TH17 cells
35959804.conclusion_quote: The data demonstrated that MW‑9 could attenuate EAE in part through suppressing the formation and activities of pathogenic T H 17 cells.
35959804.summary: In mice with EAE, a chalcone derivative called MW-9 given orally reduced disease severity and demyelination by suppressing harmful TH17 immune cells.

34911793.mechanism: Modulates S1P receptors, reducing meningeal lymphoid tissue formation
34911793.conclusion_quote: Beneficial effects on the disease course correlated with a reduction in mELT, suggesting that inhibition of mELT may be an additional mechanism of action of siponimod in the treatment of EAE.
34911793.summary: In mice with EAE, the drug siponimod reduced inflammatory lymphoid tissue in the brain coverings and improved disease when given before or during peak disease.

35313917.mechanism: suppresses chemokine and cytokine induction in neuroretina
35313917.conclusion_quote: Our data identify a combinatorial role for Nlrp12 in dampening autoimmunity of the neuroretina.
35313917.summary: In mice with experimental autoimmune uveitis, removing the innate immune gene Nlrp12 worsened eye inflammation and damage, while Nlrp12 normally suppresses retinal inflammatory signals.

36012448.conclusion_quote: Overall, it first showed that at different stages of EAE development, abzymes could significantly differ in specific sites of H4 hydrolysis.
36012448.summary: In mice with EAE, the team measured antibodies from different disease stages and found they cut histone H4 at different sites, with the most sites seen after immunization.

36052340.mechanism: Reduces microglial and astrocyte activation, raises NRF2 expression
36052340.conclusion_quote: Taken together, the data herein suggest robust attenuation of the glial response in EAE mice treated with DMF and PGB.
36052340.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, combining dimethyl fumarate and pregabalin after symptoms began reduced activated glial cells in the spinal cord more than either drug alone.

35038645.mechanism: Reduces oxidative stress and inflammation, and bacterial dysbiosis
35038645.conclusion_quote: Melatonin could play an effective role against MS, either alone or as a therapy combined with traditional agents.
35038645.summary: In rats with EAE, an animal model of MS, melatonin improved clinical signs and reduced oxidative stress, inflammation and gut bacterial imbalance.

36514132.conclusion_quote: Microglia serve multiple roles during demyelination, yet their transcriptomic state resembles other neurodegenerative conditions.
36514132.summary: In mice fed the demyelinating agent cuprizone, single-cell sequencing identified microglia that engulf dying cells, showing how these cells respond during myelin loss.

35686489.mechanism: reduces dendritic cell activation, induces antigen-specific tolerance
35686489.conclusion_quote: The dual peptide nanoparticles have great potential for the treatment of autoimmune diseases by inducing immune tolerance.
35686489.summary: In mice with EAE, a nanoparticle carrying an MS-like antigen and a co-stimulation inhibitor fully prevented disease and reduced spinal cord inflammation and nerve damage.

36364362.conclusion_quote: All of the data show that the IgG peroxidase and oxidoreductase activities of EAE mice can play an important role in their protection from toxic compounds and oxidative stress.
36364362.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, blood antibodies showed stronger peroxidase and oxidoreductase activity as disease developed, suggesting they may help protect against oxidative stress.

35937048.mechanism: Blocks serotonin reuptake, modulating immune cell function
35937048.conclusion_quote: The results of this and other studies suggest that fluoxetine could be considered an additional therapy to the standard first-line disease-modifying treatment for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
35937048.summary: This brief review discusses how the antidepressant fluoxetine may affect immune cells in multiple sclerosis and reviews retrospective patient data.

35093106.conclusion_quote: The size of the inflammatory monocyte response induced by TMEV scales with the amount of infectious virus in the initial inoculum, despite the development of equivalent peak infectious viral load.
35093106.summary: In mice infected with a brain-inflaming virus, larger doses caused more inflammatory immune cells and stronger seizures, showing that inflammation contributes to seizures rather than multiple sclerosis.

35163399.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, oxidative stress was involved in LPC-induced apoptosis, whileautophagy of mouse ovarian granulosa cells and the inhibition of autophagy could alleviate LPC-induced apoptosis.
35163399.summary: In mouse ovarian granulosa cells, not an MS model, lysophosphatidylcholine triggered cell death and autophagy, and blocking autophagy eased the damage.

35060065.conclusion_quote: These observations indicate that in the mice of both age groups a cuprizone-supplemented diet contributes to an increase in demyelination in the corpus callosum and neural progenitor cells in the dentate gyrus, although the damage is more pronounced in young adult mice.
35060065.summary: In young and aged mice, a cuprizone diet caused brain demyelination and fewer neural progenitor cells, with stronger effects in young adults.

36499195.conclusion_quote: Cellular crosstalk analysis yielded novel markers of microglia ligands, OPC receptors and target genes.
36499195.summary: In a reanalysis of cuprizone mouse and human MS gene data, researchers mapped how microglia and oligodendrocyte precursor cells communicate during demyelination and remyelination.

36004319.mechanism: Activates AhR receptor, encouraging regulatory T-cell differentiation
36004319.conclusion_quote: Kynurenine ameliorates EAE disease progression prophylactically and reduces relapses therapeutically.
36004319.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, daily kynurenine given early prevented severe disease, while later treatment reduced relapses but only helped after several weeks.

35408594.conclusion_quote: Given that these changes are harmful to mice, we believe them to cause the development of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
35408594.summary: This study examined bone marrow stem cells, immune cells and autoantibodies in 2D2 mice with spontaneous EAE, finding changes that likely contribute to the disease.

37200683.mechanism: immunosuppression and immunomodulation plus cell replacement and repair
37200683.conclusion_quote: Recent studies have proposed mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) as a new therapeutic candidate for MS.
37200683.summary: This review summarizes studies of mesenchymal stem cells as a possible treatment for multiple sclerosis, covering results in animal models and patients.

36105617.mechanism: delivers myelin protein with anti-CD20 antibody on nanoparticles
36105617.conclusion_quote: Nano-rhMBP-RTX treated group ameliorated the adverse effects induced in the EAE model.
36105617.summary: In mice with EAE, a nanoparticle carrying myelin protein and rituximab reduced symptoms, inflammation, and nerve damage, and preserved myelin better than single treatments.

36427301.conclusion_quote: Here, we directly compared CD11c + T-bet + ABCs using models of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), gammaherpesvirus 68 (γHV68), multiple sclerosis (MS), and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), and found that each drives the ABC population to opposing phenotypes.
36427301.summary: Researchers compared age-associated B cells across viral infection, mice with EAE, and people with relapsing MS, finding these cells help viruses worsen autoimmune disease.

35596557.mechanism: Cuprizone diet causes demyelination, not a treatment being tested
35596557.conclusion_quote: This is the first study to show that cortical demyelination independent of inflammation can negatively impact urinary function.
35596557.summary: In mice given the cuprizone diet, which causes brain demyelination, bladder control worsened and recovered after stopping the diet, while brainstem reflexes stayed normal.

35765518.mechanism: activates CB2 receptor, lowering inflammatory cytokines
35765518.conclusion_quote: The CB2 receptor agonist GW-405833, improves clinical conditions and reduces inflammation in mice with EAE.
35765518.summary: In mice with EAE, a CB2 receptor agonist called GW-405833 reduced inflammatory chemicals in the blood and improved movement and balance.

35805128.conclusion_quote: These findings indicate how temporal differences in immune responses are influenced by host genetic background and demonstrate the potential of serum biomarkers to track the neurological effects of viral infection.
35805128.summary: In genetically diverse mice infected with Theiler's virus, a model of demyelination, certain immune signals in blood predicted paralysis and limb weakness during acute infection.

35287559.mechanism: Inhibits microglia activation via PI3K/Akt and NF-κB signalling
35287559.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, emodin has a promising role in EAE/MS treatment, warranting further detailed studies.
35287559.summary: Mice with EAE, a model of MS, given emodin had milder symptoms, less immune cell infiltration and better myelin, linked to reduced microglia activation and inflammation.

34961984.mechanism: Suppresses TLR4, HMGB1 and NLRP3 inflammasome activation
34961984.conclusion_quote: Overall, our data suggest that tibolone may serve as a promising agent for the attenuation of MS-related inflammation.
34961984.summary: Tibolone, a synthetic hormone drug related to estrogen, was given to mice with EAE, a model of MS. It calmed inflammation, reduced myelin damage and improved neurological symptoms.

35504189.mechanism: Removing LCN2 lowers interferon gamma and cerebellar demyelination
35504189.conclusion_quote: Overall, our results support a harmful role for LCN2 in the disease context.
35504189.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the LCN2 gene did not change clinical scores but reduced inflammatory signals and myelin loss in the cerebellum.

35678041.mechanism: Immune-suppressing cells reduce Th-17 inflammatory cells
35678041.conclusion_quote: Pre- and post-treatment of immunized mice by Tregs, MDSCs and IL-2 prevent EAE induction.
35678041.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, treatment with regulatory T cells, MDSCs and IL-2 before or after immunization reduced Th-17 cells and disease signs.

35090883.mechanism: Activates SIRT1 signaling, reducing inflammation and apoptosis
35090883.conclusion_quote: This study provides a potential candidate for treating MS.
35090883.summary: In mice with EAE, a model of MS, pterostilbene reduced inflammation and damage in the optic nerves and retina by activating the SIRT1 pathway.

35018577.mechanism: Binds TSPO, boosts neurosteroid allopregnanolone production
35018577.conclusion_quote: Altogether, our results suggest that PIGA1138-based treatment may represent an interesting possibility to be explored for the innovation of effective therapies against PPMS.
35018577.summary: In mice with EAE, a TSPO ligand called PIGA1138 reduced disease symptoms, preserved myelin and nerve fibers, and lowered immune cell infiltration into the brain and spinal cord.

36210459.mechanism: No treatment tested, biomarker detection only
36210459.conclusion_quote: While NfL levels were elevated later in the pathogenesis of the DTH lesion, serum and CSF metabolomics were able to detect early, clinically silent neuroinflammation and are likely to present sensitive biomarkers for the assessment of subclinical disease activity in patients.
36210459.summary: In rats with a delayed-type hypersensitivity model of MS, blood and spinal fluid metabolite changes detected hidden inflammation earlier than the nerve damage marker neurofilament light chain.

36028771.conclusion_quote: Together, this dataset provides a resource for immunologists that can be integrated with future single-cell immune repertoire and transcriptome sequencing datasets.
36028771.summary: This study profiled immune cell receptors and gene activity in mice with EAE, a model of MS, and in virus-infected mice, providing a shared resource for immunologists.

35268192.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, lysolecithin supplementation in sows resulted in improved litter weight at weaning without an excessive catabolism of backfat tissue, most probably due to an efficient nutrient utilization, which warrants further investigation.
35268192.summary: Sows fed a lysolecithin diet supplement had heavier litters at weaning and lost less backfat, with no multiple sclerosis model involved.

34668659.mechanism: Reduces seizures through varied antiseizure and anti-inflammatory mechanisms
34668659.conclusion_quote: Compounds reducing seizures in the TMEV comprise distinct mechanistic classes, some with mechanisms of action that extend beyond traditional ASMs.
34668659.summary: In mice infected with Theiler's virus, several antiseizure drugs and anti-inflammatory drugs reduced seizures, with phenobarbital and valproate working best.

35611900.conclusion_quote: Macrophages are central to the functioning of the innate immune response and, depending on the phenotype, have pro-and anti-inflammatory properties.
35611900.summary: This review explains how macrophages, immune cells of the nervous system, can either drive or calm inflammation in multiple sclerosis and its animal model.

35496821.mechanism: depletes CD52-expressing lymphocytes, causing prolonged T cell lymphopenia
35496821.conclusion_quote: These data demonstrate that thymus function can alter the effectiveness of anti-CD52 treatment.
35496821.summary: In mice with EAE, removing the thymus before anti-CD52 treatment prolonged loss of CD4 T cells and caused relapses in about two-thirds of the mice.

36498875.mechanism: binds RORγt, blocking its transcriptional activity
36498875.conclusion_quote: Collectively, these results demonstrated TDC targeting RORγt to suppress Th17 cell polarization, as well as its activity, thus, indicating the potential of this compound in treating of Th17-related autoimmune disorders and organ transplant rejection disorders.
36498875.summary: In mice with EAE, an animal model of MS, a natural compound called 2,2',4'-trihydroxychalcone reduced harmful immune cells and eased disease symptoms.

35930635.mechanism: Blocks G9a, restoring anti-ferroptotic gene expression
35930635.conclusion_quote: This study identifies G9a as a critical transcriptional enhancer of neuronal ferroptosis and potential therapeutic target to counteract inflammation-induced neurodegeneration.
35930635.summary: In mice with EAE and human MS tissue, blocking the G9a enzyme restored protective genes, reduced nerve cell loss and improved disease outcome.

35141565.mechanism: Not applicable, methods protocol without a tested treatment
35141565.conclusion_quote: Here, we present a protocol to consistently measure the volume of demyelination and remyelination in mice following brain lysolecithin injections.
35141565.summary: This methods paper describes a protocol that measures the volume of demyelination and remyelination in mice with brain lesions induced by lysolecithin injection.

36525604.conclusion_quote: However, the evidence for this is indirect and insufficient.
36525604.summary: This review summarizes studies of CD8+ IL17+ (Tc17) T cells in multiple sclerosis, EAE and other autoimmune diseases, and finds the evidence for their role is indirect and insufficient.

36552864.mechanism: Inhibits spermine oxidase, reducing neuroinflammation and oxidative damage
36552864.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, our studies demonstrate the potential benefits of targeting SMOX to treat MS-mediated neuroinflammation and vision loss.
36552864.summary: In mice with EAE, a drug blocking the enzyme SMOX reduced retinal nerve cell loss, optic nerve inflammation, and motor problems while improving vision.

35046083.mechanism: reduces microglial inflammatory activation and iron content
35046083.conclusion_quote: Together, our data indicate that DMF-induced reduction of susceptibility in MS lesions is associated with a decreased activation state in microglial cells.
35046083.summary: In a study of 34 patients with MS and human microglia grown in lab dishes, dimethyl fumarate reduced iron and inflammation in chronic active lesions compared with glatiramer acetate.

36426970.mechanism: Blocks T-cell priming and antibody production
36426970.conclusion_quote: These data demonstrate that CD40 supports distinct effector programs in B cells and DCs that converge to drive a CNS autoimmune disease and identify targets for intervention.
36426970.summary: In mice with EAE, removing CD40 from dendritic cells or B cells reduced disease, showing CD40 drives inflammation through T cells and antibodies.

35525327.mechanism: Restores circadian clock gene expression and immune regulation
35525327.conclusion_quote: Our study suggested that the pathogenesis of pSS might correlate with abnormal expression of circadian genes, and that melatonin might be a potential candidate for prevention and treatment of pSS.
35525327.summary: In a mouse model of Sjögren's syndrome, an autoimmune disease affecting tear and saliva glands, melatonin improved gland function and reduced inflammation.

35526486.mechanism: Blocks dendritic cell activation and NF-κB phosphorylation
35526486.conclusion_quote: This work displayed that AA possessed a potential anti-inflammatory therapeutic effect for the treatment of autoimmune disease.
35526486.summary: In mice with EAE, an MS model, anacardic acid reduced immune cell infiltration into the spinal cord and protected myelin from damage.

35704993.mechanism: cDC1 IDO1 kynurenine induces tolerogenic cDC2 cells
35704993.conclusion_quote: This study identifies a previously unrecognized metabolic communication in which IDO1-expressing cDC1 cells extend their immunoregulatory capacity to the cDC2 subset through their production of tryptophan metabolite l-kynurenine.
35704993.summary: In mice with EAE, removing IDO1 from cDC1 immune cells worsened disease, showing these cells help calm inflammation via kynurenine.

36269826.mechanism: Blocks RORγt binding and activation of Runx1 expression
36269826.conclusion_quote: Thus, RORγt regulates the effector function of T H 17 cells in addition to T H 17 differentiation.
36269826.summary: In mice with EAE, a mutation that prevents RORγt ubiquitination left Th17 cell development intact but greatly reduced disease severity.

interventions: peptide-MHCII chimeric antigen receptor (pMHCII-CAR) T cells
36206355.mechanism: Depletes MOG-specific CD4 T cells via CAR targeting
36206355.conclusion_quote: Thus, these data suggest a model in which higher-affinity autoreactive T cells are required to provide the "activation energy" for initiating neuroinflammatory injury, but lower-affinity cells are sufficient to maintain ongoing disease.
36206355.summary: In mice with EAE, CAR T cells that deplete MOG-specific CD4 T cells prevented disease and reversed ongoing paralysis, showing lower-affinity cells help sustain the illness.

36496888.mechanism: Upregulates growth-related and nutrient transporter gene expression
36496888.conclusion_quote: In conclusion, upregulating the nutrients transporter gene and growth-related gene expression of the host, independent of nutrition level changes, may be the action mechanism of lysolecithin on growth promotion in animals.
36496888.summary: In broiler chickens, adding lysolecithin to feed boosted weight gain and nutrient absorption, but the study does not involve multiple sclerosis or demyelination.

35536649.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes disease mechanism
35536649.conclusion_quote: Taken together, our data show that while Th17 cells initiate CNS inflammation, subsequent clinical symptoms and gray matter pathology are dictated by age and associated with other immune cells, such as neutrophils.
35536649.summary: In old and young SJL/J mice with passive EAE, age shaped lasting brain inflammation and gray matter damage, with neutrophils linked to these changes.

interventions: Genomic deletion of Mincle in T cells
35504893.mechanism: blocks glucosylceramide synthesis, reducing Mincle-driven T cell inflammation
35504893.conclusion_quote: Taken together, this study indicates that sensing of danger signals by Mincle on TH17 cells plays a critical role in promoting CNS inflammation.
35504893.summary: In mice with EAE, deleting the Mincle sensor from T cells or blocking its natural ligand production reduced harmful inflammatory cells and slowed disease progression.

35573205.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes disease mechanism
35573205.conclusion_quote: These data suggest that the adventitious concurrence of immune-mediated neurodegenerative traits by Eomes + Th cells and ectopic expression of L1-derived antigen(s) in the inflamed CNS may materialize a communal and previously unappreciated pathogenesis of neurodegeneration.
35573205.summary: In mice with EAE, ALS, and Alzheimer's models, certain immune T cells and reactivated LINE-1 gene elements appear to together drive nerve cell loss in the brain and spinal cord.

35859078.mechanism: Describes glial cell distribution during aging and remyelination
35859078.conclusion_quote: These results suggest that the presence of microglia is important for the characteristic cell localization pattern of LAs.
35859078.summary: In aging mice and mice with chemically induced demyelination, researchers mapped glial cell arrangements in the corpus callosum and found microglia help form cell clusters.

35185870.mechanism: No treatment tested, describes B cell response
35185870.conclusion_quote: Our study demonstrates the pre-clinical mobilization of the MOG-specific B cell response within the brain-draining cervical lymph nodes, and reiterates that MOG antibodies are a poor biomarker of disease onset and progression.
35185870.summary: In a spontaneous mouse model of EAE, MOG specific B cells gather in brain draining neck lymph nodes before disease starts, and MOG antibodies poorly predict disease onset.
